Build ein_key: every identifier an EIN holds, with how specific it is

Source: R/md-ein-key.R
md_build_ein_key.Rd

One long table of the keys a matcher can block on, so a hard case can find candidates through something other than its name: a shared place or a website. One row per (ein, kind, key).

Usage

md_build_ein_key(con = NULL)

Arguments

con

A connection from md_db().

Value

Rows per kind, invisibly.

Details

name

name_key from name_compact - legal, dba, observed and former names, without in-care-of names or guarded observed rows

place

street_key|zip5 from address_compact

website

site_key from website, kind = 'url'

email_domain

site_key from website, kind = 'email'

person

an officer, director or key employee's name key from person_key (md_ingest_officers()), when that table exists

How specific a key is

n_eins_sharing counts the EINs holding the key, across the whole database. A key held by one EIN can propose a candidate on its own; a key held by thousands (1 WATERFOWL WAY|38120, ptk.org) can only confirm one found another way.

The whole-database count answers "is this key ambiguous in the universe". A matcher comparing against a selection of layers needs the count within the selection, so md_build_ein_key() also writes ein_key_layer: the count per (kind, key, layer). Layers partition EINs - each EIN has exactly one - so the count for any set of layers is the exact sum of its rows.

Rebuild after its inputs

Derived from name_compact, address_compact and website, so it is rebuilt after them, by DROP and CREATE.
